6:bulkley-river:bulkley-river-and-morice.why: Owner 2026-11-09 (round 7): "for morice river i cant add bulkley to extents … for the forks it is needed … bulkley 100m up to 1000m down on bulkley too". DFO's own words for this place: "waters within the four white triangular fishing boundary signs located at the confluence of the Bulkley River and Morice River … The closure starts 100 meters upstream of the confluence and ends approximately 1 kilometre downstream" — so the distances are DFO's (100 m up each arm, about 1 km down), not ours. The whole zone as 2 pieces on EXISTING built cuts, no new cut: the Morice's last 100 m (morice_river__bulkley_confluence_u100m → morice_river__bulkley_confluence) and the Bulkley from 100 m up the upper Bulkley to 1 km below the confluence (bulkley_river__morice_river_into_bulkley_river_u100m → …_d1000m; in FWA the water below the confluence is the Bulkley). Tributaries excluded on both pieces: a short piece 'including tributaries' would walk the whole system above it. This place's extent now is the Bulkley piece only; the proposal ADDS the Morice piece, so either wording alone shows the whole zone.
6:bulkley-river:bulkley-river-and-morice.by: claude, from DFO's words + the owner's round-7 words; replaces the 11-09 one-water proposal

suggestion.words: the whole Forks zone, 2 pieces: the Bulkley from 100 m up the upper Bulkley to 1 km below the confluence + the Morice's last 100 m; no tributaries

6:sheldens-creek:upstream-of-white-trian.why: Owner's problem report 2026-11-09 (T571): "i think spur 19 is at completely the wrong spot?". WHERE THE CUT CAME FROM: the forest-tenure road 'SP 19(1) TO SHELDONS' (FTEN R06206 section 331) crosses the stream at 53.12968,-131.78224 — 3.4 km up a 3.7 km stream, so 'upstream of' it is only the top 290 m. WHAT THE DATA SHOWS: BC's road atlas has three roads crossing this stream — 130 m above the mouth at Sheldens Bay (53.14853,-131.76517), at the present cut, and near the source; it names no 'Spur 19' anywhere on Moresby Island (the named roads beside the creek are Spur 20 and Spur 20C), and the stream itself is our match, not a named Sheldens Creek. So the data cannot say which crossing DFO's 'Spur 19 Bridge site' is. THIS PROPOSAL is the other candidate: the road crossing 130 m above the mouth, which makes the closure nearly the whole creek. It is a low-confidence alternative for you to look at on the map, not a finding. If neither is right, place it yourself: Edit this extent → new cuts → point → click the creek (or drag the orange marker).
6:sheldens-creek:upstream-of-white-trian.by: claude, from BC's Digital Road Atlas and forest-tenure roads (T571)
